notes: Източниците по-горе се препоръчват начални точки и подкрепят съответната методическа дискусия; за тази глава са създадени измислени казуси и числени упражнения. Главата обяснява установените понятия на достъпен език и не е твърдение, че едно проучване или един метод решава всеки оспорван въпрос за научни изследвания.

002.title: Препоръчани източници

entries.html: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Informal Logic.” A scholarly overview of informal argument evaluation, acceptability, relevance and sufficiency. https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/logic-informal/
Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Fallacies.” A comprehensive reference emphasizing that labels must be justified by identifying the actual reasoning error. https://iep.utm.edu/fallacy/

OpenStax, Introduction to Philosophy, Chapter 5, especially “5.3 Arguments,” “5.4 Types of Inferences,” and “5.5 Informal Fallacies.” Free introductory textbook on validity, reasoning types and common errors. https://openstax.org/books/introduction-philosophy/pages/5-introduction
Stephen Toulmin, The Uses of Argument (1958; later editions). Influential treatment of claims, grounds, warrants, backing, qualifiers and rebuttals.
Anthony Weston, A Rulebook for Arguments (various editions). A compact, accessible introduction to constructing and scrutinizing arguments.

David Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, Book III, Part I, Section I. Classic discussion relevant to the transition from descriptive to normative claims; read alongside modern commentary rather than as a complete contemporary treatment.

notes: В центъра на града и слънчевите сценарии са изградени учебни примери, а не открития за конкретен град или проект. Източниците по-горе подкрепят основните концепции на главата и осигуряват по-нататъшно проучване; това е синтез, а не научна литература преглед. По-късните глави относно историята, икономиката и политиката ще предоставят свои собствени конкретни доказателства.

entries.html: OpenStax. Introductory Statistics 2e, especially chapters on probability, random variables, sampling, and confidence intervals. Free open textbook: https://openstax.org/details/books/introductory-statistics-2e

Diez, Çetinkaya-Rundel and Barr. OpenIntro Statistics, fourth edition. Chapters on probability, inference, and data collection. Free textbook and companion resources: https://www.openintro.org/book/os/
NIST/SEMATECH. e-Handbook of Statistical Methods. A more advanced and methodical reference for measurement, uncertainty, statistical design, and reliability: https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/
National Weather Service. Forecast Terms. A useful official definition of probability of precipitation and its time and location conditions: https://www.weather.gov/ppg/forecast_terms
Gigerenzer, Gerd. Risk Savvy: How to Make Good Decisions (2014). An accessible exploration of communicating risks in natural frequencies and avoiding statistical misunderstandings.
Hacking, Ian. An Introduction to Probability and Inductive Logic (2001). A readable and careful introduction to interpreting chance, inference, and evidence.

Silver, Nate. The Signal and the Noise: Why So Many Predictions Fail—but Some Don't (2012). Forecasting, model assumptions, and the difficulty of making predictions in messy fields. Read critically, as with any author's particular examples and interpretations.

004.title: Препоръчани източници и допълнително четене

entries.html: Library of Congress. Teacher's Guides and Analysis Tool: Getting Started with Primary Sources. Clear prompts for observation, reflection, and questioning; useful with manuscripts, images, oral accounts, maps, and newspapers. https://www.loc.gov/programs/teachers/getting-started-with-primary-sources/guides/
John Tosh. The Pursuit of History, revised editions. A readable introduction to historical questions, sources, interpretation, explanation, and research practice.
Martha Howell and Walter Prevenier. From Reliable Sources: An Introduction to Historical Methods (2001). A thoughtful guide to source criticism, context, and how historians build arguments.
Marc Bloch. The Historian's Craft. A classic introduction to asking questions of historical traces; read it as a formative statement of method, not a substitute for newer research.

Oxford Radiocarbon Accelerator Unit, University of Oxford. What is Radiocarbon Dating? Explains sample selection, calibration, conventional BP dates, old wood, and contamination. https://www.arch.ox.ac.uk/oxford-radiocarbon-accelerator-unit
University of Oxford. Radiocarbon Calibration. Why an uncalibrated radiocarbon age is not a calendar date, including historical conventions used in reporting. https://c14.arch.ox.ac.uk/calibration

UK Parliament. The Making of Magna Carta. An institutional explanation of the surviving 1215 copies and how they were produced. https://www.parliament.uk/about/living-heritage/evolutionofparliament/2015-parliament-in-the-making/2015-historic-anniversaries/magna-carta/the-making-of-magna-carta-/
J. C. Holt. Magna Carta (2nd ed., 1992), especially the analysis of the 1215 documents and changing interpretations. Scholarly treatment, not a simple legend.
UNESCO World Heritage Centre. Great Zimbabwe National Monument. The site's archaeology, period, setting, and historical significance. https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/364/

The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Great Zimbabwe (11th–15th Century). A museum explanation of the site's construction and the problems caused by colonial-era interpretations. https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/great-zimbabwe-11th-15th-century

Government of Bulgaria, Council of Ministers. History. Concise official chronology for the treaties of 1878, Unification in 1885, and independence in 1908. https://www.government.bg/en/About-Bulgaria/HISTORY/tabsss1

National Museum of Military History, Bulgaria. Declaring the Independence of Bulgaria (1908). Context and historical documents for the declaration and recognition process. https://militarymuseum.bg/en/exhibitions/chronological-exhibition/declaring-the-independence-of-bulgaria-1908/

United States Holocaust Memorial Museum. Evidence from the Holocaust at the First Nuremberg Trial. A demonstration of how perpetrator documents and other evidence establish historical events. https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/evidence-from-the-holocaust
Royal Observatory of Belgium. The Gregorian Calendar. Calendar reform and adoption across different places. https://robinfo.oma.be/en/astro-info/calendar/the-gregorian-calendar/

notes: Интерпретативните примери са обяснения, а не цитати от исторически документи. Измисленият град и хипотетичните сценарии са измислени за практика. Връзките по-горе се препоръчват начални точки; изданието за публикуване следва да добави цитати на ниво страница за точни искания, да се консултира със специалист стипендия за спорни въпроси и да прегледа историографията с развитието на поредицата от статии.

notes: Опростените цифрови примери в настоящата глава са изрично илюстративни. Диаграмаите са концептуални, а не изследователски карти или прогнози. Спорните политически граници следва да бъдат проучени с имена, датирани и ясно определени изходни карти. Описаните тук глобални географски отношения са предназначени да останат полезни дори когато индивидуалната инфраструктура, търговска или климатична статистика се промени.
